newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK SE, SYNDICATE TO SIGN LOAN GUARANTEE DEAL.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK SE, SYNDICATE TO SIGN LOAN GUARANTEE DEAL.

text.p: Slovak state monopoly electrical utility Slovenske Elektrarne a.s. (SE) said on Friday it had reached an agreement with a consortium of international banks to guarantee a 15-year, 70 million ECU loan by the European Investment Bank (EIB).

The loan, signed last November, will be priced when the funds are drawn at a level covering the EIB's costs for obtaining the credit. Funds from the credit will be used for the upgrading of a power plant at Vojany, eastern Slovakia.
"The EIB had originally expected the loan to be state- guaranteed, but this appeared impossible," Viera Dekysova, director of SE's financial relations department, told Reuters.
"(But) SE has already received state guarantees for loans for the construction of the Mochovce nuclear plant, therefore the company had to ask the international banking community," she added.

Banks which will provide both the guarantee and loan are the Bank of America, the Sumitomo Bank, the Bank of Tokyo Mitsubishi, Bayerishe Landesbank, Credit Suisse First Boston, Dresdner Bank Lux., ING Barings, J.P.Morgan Securities, NatWest Capital Markets and Bank Austria.
Chase Manhattan, Citibank, Norichukin Bank and Tokai Bank will also participate in the loan syndicate, but are not members of the guarantee syndicate.
The loan puts the total amount of financing SE obtained in 1996 for its investment programme at 50 billion crowns.
SE officials have said the loan is expected to be followed in 1999 by another 65 million ECU tranche from EIB for the same project. -- Peter Javurek, Bratislava Newsroom, 421-7-521-8402
